company_description: Electronic Arts Inc. develops, markets, publishes, and delivers games, content, and services for game consoles, PCs, and mobile phones worldwide. It develops and publishes games and services across various genres, such as sports, racing, first-person shooter, action, role-playing, and simulation; and live services offerings, including extra content and subscription offerings through its global football and American football franchises, such as EA SPORTS College Football and EA SPORTS Madden NFL, as well as based on its IP comprising The Sims, Apex Legends, and Battlefield. The company markets and sells its games and services through digital distribution and retail channels; and directly to mass market retailers, specialty stores, and distribution arrangements. Electronic Arts Inc. was incorporated in 1982 and is headquartered in Redwood City, California.

risks.title: Intense competition in the video game industry
risks.summary: The video game market is highly competitive and rapidly evolving. EA must continuously innovate and anticipate trends to remain relevant against established competitors and new entrants.
risks.score_rationale: The text explicitly mentions the intense and fast-paced competition in the video game market, emphasizing that success depends on anticipating changes. Competition is a key industry factor, with players having greater financial resources. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Dependence on distribution platforms
risks.summary: EA relies on consoles (Sony, Microsoft) and mobile app stores (Apple, Google) to distribute its games. These platforms can unilaterally change their terms, threatening EA's revenue.
risks.score_rationale: EA heavily depends on partners such as Sony and Microsoft for console distribution, and Apple/Google for mobile. These agreements are subject to unilateral changes and can be terminated in the short term, directly impacting revenue. Direct sales represent 39% (Sony) and 17% (Microsoft) of total revenue in 2025. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Rapid technological evolution and AI
risks.summary: The industry is rapidly advancing technologically, particularly with AI. EA must invest heavily in R&D to integrate these innovations and maintain game quality and appeal.
risks.score_rationale: The text highlights the need to invest in R&D to keep up with technological advances, especially AI, to remain competitive. Failure to adapt quickly could harm product quality and innovation. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Complex and evolving regulatory environment
risks.summary: EA must navigate a complex and constantly changing global regulatory landscape (privacy, data, virtual gaming). These changes can restrict its operations or business models.
risks.score_rationale: EA is subject to complex and changing laws worldwide regarding data protection, privacy, online safety, and business models (games with virtual items). Regulatory uncertainty can impact operations and revenue. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Intellectual property protection
risks.summary: Protecting EA's intellectual property is crucial but challenging, especially internationally. Weaker laws in certain countries and counterfeiting risks threaten its creative assets.
risks.score_rationale: EA relies on intellectual property (IP) but faces challenges in protecting it, particularly in certain Asian countries where laws are less protective or poorly enforced. IP disputes can be costly and damage reputation. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Dependence on popular franchises and Ultimate Team
risks.summary: A significant portion of EA's revenue comes from specific game modes such as Ultimate Team in its sports franchises. A decline in popularity or issues with these modes would have a major financial impact.
risks.score_rationale: EA's success relies heavily on key franchises such as EA SPORTS FC and Madden NFL, and specifically on the Ultimate Team mode. A decline in popularity or issues with these modes/franchises would have a material impact. The 10-K confirms that Ultimate Team revenues are 'material to our business'. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Security and reliability of technology infrastructure
risks.summary: With the growth of online gaming, the security and reliability of EA's technology infrastructure are essential. Cyberattacks or security breaches could harm player experience and the company's reputation.
risks.score_rationale: The growth of EA's digital business makes the company dependent on the reliability and security of its technology infrastructure. Abuse and security issues can affect player experience and reputation. (default score, to be refined)

ai_positioning.summary: EA recognizes the importance of rapid technological evolution, including AI, and emphasizes the need to invest heavily in R&D to integrate these innovations and maintain competitiveness, according to the 10-K.
evidence: 10-K text mentions 'Rapid technological evolution and AI' as a risk factor
Commitment to R&D to keep up with technological advances including AI
